name: The Fool — the Wayfarer
tagline: The unconditioned mind: innocent, and ready to learn the wide world without prejudice.
meaning: Zero is the emptiness from which everything begins. A sudden new journey, leaving bonds and the past behind, trusting instinct and stepping into the unknown carrying neither fear nor bias. The pure energy of freedom. The deck paints him as a young traveller in plain hemp with a small bundle and a loyal dog, walking happily through misty, flowering valleys — not foolish, simply free of society’s frames.
caution: Innocence overdone becomes foolishness. Beware naïve optimism, impulsive and irresponsible decisions, and “live for today” spending with no backup plan.
koan: The empty mind is the most powerful mind — ready to learn, and capable of anything.
universalUpright: New beginnings, spontaneity, faith, a leap into the unknown
universalReversed: Recklessness, naïveté, hesitation, risk without a safety net
integration: Both systems agree on the leap. The Tao layer turns “fool” into “empty vessel”: go, but travel light of assumptions rather than light of planning.

name: The Magician
tagline: Using talent and intellect to create — with integrity.
meaning: A Taoist adept or learned sage stands at an altar of ancient texts, astronomical instruments and the symbols of the five elements, with the character 道 glowing behind him under the moon while white cranes dance. Brilliant intellect, singular gifts, fast learning, and success that starts when you act skilfully with your own hands.
caution: Wit and eloquence without truthful speech (信) turn into manipulation for personal gain. Also warns against being broad but shallow — dabbling in many things and finishing none.
koan: When wisdom joins with truthful speech, all things can be conjured at will.
universalReversed: Manipulation, trickery, scattered talent, untapped potential
integration: The universal card says “you have the tools”. This deck adds the condition: the tools only work cleanly when word and deed match. Check the integrity of the plan before its cleverness.

name: The High Priestess
tagline: Stillness and intuition; understanding the truth that lives within.
meaning: A noble woman in pure white robes meditates among mountains and a sacred waterfall, the character 智 above her amid a dharma wheel and white cranes, a glowing orb in her hands. Accurate intuition, secrets not yet revealed, stillness that subdues movement, and trust in the warning voice from deep within.
caution: Sinking too far into your private emotional world until you become repressed, brooding or cut off from reality. Also indecision, emotion ruling reason, and hidden matters that cause discomfort later.
koan: When body and mind are still as clear water, all truth appears without a word.
universalUpright: Intuition, the subconscious, mystery, inner knowing
universalReversed: Secrets, disconnection from intuition, withdrawal, repressed feeling
integration: Near-identical meanings. The still-water image is a useful practice cue: don’t force the answer; let the sediment settle and it shows itself.

name: The Empress
tagline: The mother who gives life — warmth, abundance and compassion.
meaning: An empress in blue-and-white robes cradles her child amid waterfalls, blooming peonies, wild deer and dancing cranes. Fertile feminine energy, birth and flourishing, patronage from elders, and a season of physical and emotional comfort.
caution: Love and protection overdone become control or spoiling. Also warns of laziness, a love of comfort that neglects duty, and indulgent spending.
koan: Pure compassion nourishes and grows like fertile earth.
universalUpright: Abundance, nurturing, fertility, creativity, sensual comfort
universalReversed: Smothering, dependence, creative block, neglect of self or others
integration: Same card, seen through 仁: abundance is meant to be given without expecting return. Reversed, read the caution — care that has turned into control.

name: The Emperor
tagline: Order and custom; doing your duty as a good leader.
meaning: The supreme ruler stands firm among steep peaks and ranks of soldiers, banners bearing auspicious characters, officials kneeling in order, a crane overhead. Commanding masculine energy, decisiveness, governance and discipline — someone others can rely on.
caution: Using power on a whim; rules held so tightly you become a stubborn autocrat who won’t listen. Unbending hardness makes people uneasy, drives them away, or breeds quiet resistance.
koan: A leader rules not by decree but wins hearts through ethics and discipline.
universalReversed: Tyranny, rigidity, domination, lack of discipline
integration: The Confucian twist: authority is legitimate only through correct conduct (禮), not position. Pair with the Hierophant, the other 禮 card, for questions of institutions and hierarchy.

name: The Hierophant
tagline: Honouring elders and teachers; carrying on the ancestors’ teaching.
meaning: A compassionate grand master sits on a ritual dais, an ancient text in one hand, the other raised in blessing over disciples kneeling with joined palms in a sacred valley. Spiritual wisdom, virtue, tradition, religious study, and protection from the sacred or from elders.
caution: Clinging to old frames, outdated customs or scripture until you become rigid and fusty; playing the know-it-all who lectures and judges others by your own beliefs.
koan: The wisdom of the past guides the spirit into the future.
universalUpright: Tradition, institutions, mentorship, shared belief, convention
integration: Universally “the establishment”; here, specifically your teachers, elders and lineage. Ask whose guidance you are being asked to honour — or to outgrow.

name: The Lovers
tagline: Bonds and choices built on sincerity.
meaning: A young man and woman in indigo robes gaze deeply at each other and hold hands tenderly; peonies bloom, a waterfall pours, paired cranes fly — yin and yang fused into one. Pure friendship, cooperation, harmony, and above all the card of life’s important choices.
caution: Letting passing emotion and pleasure steer; hesitating at a crossroads and wanting both paths; temptation leading you astray until you lose sincerity toward yourself and others.
koan: When yin and yang unite in sincerity, ten thousand li of obstacles collapse.
universalUpright: Love, union, aligned values, a significant choice
universalReversed: Disharmony, imbalance, misaligned values, temptation, indecision
integration: Both systems stress choice over romance. The Tao test for any union — romantic or business — is sincerity (信) on both sides.

name: The Chariot
tagline: Determination to overcome obstacles and reach the goal.
meaning: A young general in steel armour drives a war chariot pulled by four horses, black and white alternating — conflicting yin and yang harnessed to drive forward. Supreme resolve, victory earned by sweat, firm command of emotion and circumstance, long journeys and trail-blazing.
caution: Hot-headedness and stubbornness; winning through temper; charging the goal while ignoring others, which makes enemies and breakage. Also warns of accumulated stress and overwork.
koan: True gold fears no fire; a brave warrior fears no obstacle ten thousand li long.
universalReversed: Loss of control, aggression, scattered effort, burnout
integration: Rider-Waite uses a black and a white sphinx; this deck uses black and white horses — the same yin–yang reins. Victory comes from steering opposites, not suppressing one.

name: Strength
tagline: Whoever conquers himself is strong; gentleness subdues aggression.
meaning: A calm warrior sits beside a white lion and strokes its head tenderly; the wild beast yields completely to gentleness amid mist, waterfall and a glowing lantern. Not physical force but mindful mastery of instinct, anger and desire, and patience that calms hostile people and problems.
caution: Bottling feelings until they turn into chronic stress; letting base emotions break loose and hurt others; controlling people or situations behind a well-meaning face.
koan: One who conquers the self and subdues enemies with gentleness is the strongest in all the martial world.
universalUpright: Inner strength, courage, compassion, patience, self-control
integration: A perfect match with the Tao Te Ching’s teaching that the soft overcomes the hard. Numbered 8 as in Rider-Waite (Marseille decks place it at 11).

name: The Hermit
tagline: Withdrawing to train the mind and find true wisdom.
meaning: A white-bearded master meditates on a high crag, cupping a soft golden orb of wisdom, surrounded by mist, peaks, waterfall, scrolls and cranes. A pause for self-review, the search for inner truth, higher insight, and stillness that lets thoughts settle.
caution: Isolating so much that you become lonely and cut off; stubborn attachment to your own views; turning fusty, or brooding in circular thoughts.
koan: Read ten thousand books — yet without turning to the mirror, you never know your own mind.
universalUpright: Introspection, solitude, inner guidance, seeking truth
integration: Identical in spirit. The lantern becomes a golden orb and the mountain retreat of the Taoist sage.

name: Wheel of Fortune
tagline: Everything rises and falls — a law of nature no one escapes.
meaning: A traveller in soft white robes sits contemplating on a round sacred stone; the sky splits into sun on the left and crescent moon on the right; peaks, a pavilion in mist and cloth banners in ancient script surround him. Turning points, the rhythm of life, changing fortune, and large unexpected opportunities arriving by natural karmic law.
caution: At the height, don’t be careless or proud; at the bottom, don’t despair. Everything changes. Release what you cannot control, keep the mind supple, and flow with nature rather than forcing against fate.
koan: Every change hides a great opportunity.
universalUpright: Cycles, fate, turning point, luck, karma
universalReversed: Bad luck, resisting change, breaking a cycle
integration: Same card. The sun-and-moon sky makes the Wheel explicitly yin–yang: its message is timing. At a high, prepare; at a low, wait.

name: Justice
tagline: Honesty and impartial justice — do good, receive good; do evil, receive evil.
meaning: A divine lawkeeper or handsome young magistrate in finely patterned white robes holds a sword of authority pointed downward — decisive wisdom that cuts through bias and worldly desire. Rightness, reasoned decisions free of emotion, honesty, legal agreements, and karma allotting results to every act.
caution: Becoming so certain of your own views that you turn hard and merciless; judging others harshly by your standard breeds conflict. The results of past actions, good and bad, are on their way and hard to avoid.
koan: Heaven’s net is vast and its mesh is wide, yet nothing slips through. Every act has its price.
universalUpright: Fairness, truth, cause and effect, law, accountability
integration: The key phrase echoes Tao Te Ching ch. 73 (天網恢恢，疏而不漏). The scales are gone; judgement here is a lowered blade that cuts away bias. Numbered 11 as in Rider-Waite.

name: The Hanged Man
tagline: Enduring hardship to change perspective and purify the mind.
meaning: A serene young warrior hangs upside down from an ancient peach tree in full blossom, palms joined in prayer, amid mist and waterfall. Stillness as ascetic practice: patience, willingly giving up worldly comfort for a while to flip your view and free the spirit from old frames.
caution: Staying in limbo so long it becomes wasted time, or becoming a willing victim of a situation. Check whether the sacrifice is worth what you gain, or whether you are just carrying other people’s problems.
koan: When the outer world stops, the inner mind sees the world from a different angle.
integration: Matches closely. The peach tree — the tree of the immortals in Chinese lore — makes the pause sacred rather than punitive.

name: Death
tagline: The end of the old to open the way for the new; nothing lasts.
meaning: A young warrior in white stands with his back turned; his body is becoming a skeleton that dissolves into particles of energy. The end of a cycle — shedding ego, desire and whatever no longer serves — to enter shedding, cleansing and rebirth from the ashes.
caution: Clinging to the past, old habits or what has already died only makes the change longer and more painful. Accept it, take the pain to end it, and move forward without looking back at the ruins.
koan: Let the withered leaves fall, and the tree sprouts new shoots and branches.
universalReversed: Resistance to change, stagnation, fear of endings
integration: Same card; neither system reads literal death as a rule. Here the transformation is drawn directly — the ego-body dissolving into energy.

name: Temperance
tagline: Keeping life in balance; blending conflict into harmony.
meaning: A dignified young warrior sits cross-legged on a sacred stone above the water, both palms up, holding two orbs of opposite energy in balance. Gradual adjustment and change, merging conflict, and living by the wisdom of the middle way to restore smoothness.
caution: Restlessness, flip-flopping without a position, stalemate through indecision. Avoid extremes and brute force; pushing while the surrounding energies are unsettled will ruin the plan. Take time to adapt and compromise.
koan: When yin and yang are balanced, everything in life flows without obstruction.
integration: The universal angel pours water between two cups; here the warrior holds yin and yang — the Doctrine of the Mean made visible.

name: The Devil
tagline: Greed, anger and delusion that bind us to suffering and the cycle of rebirth.
meaning: A young warrior kneels clutching his temples in torment and confusion. The card of inner craving: obsession with the senses, addiction, worldly gain that drags the mind down — knowing it is bad yet unable to stop, bound by chains of desire you forged yourself.
caution: Giving in to desire; greed that breaks your morals; vice, informal high-interest debt and passing temptations. Pull your awareness back and break the chains — the cage holding you is nothing but your own wanting.
koan: Ten thousand outer demons cannot tempt a mind free of greed and delusion.
universalReversed: Release, breaking free, reclaiming power, facing the shadow
integration: No devil appears on the card: the demon is internal. The universal reversed meaning — breaking the chains — is exactly what the book’s caution urges.

name: The Tower
tagline: Whatever is built on wrongness must eventually fall.
meaning: A young warrior on a cliff grips his sword and watches lightning smash a great ancient Chinese tower until its brick and stone shatter. Sudden, earth-turning change; unstable foundations destroyed in an instant, leading to awakening and a fresh start built on truth.
caution: Sudden calamity, careless decisions, attachment to rank and praise. Keep a backup plan, don’t trust false security, and when change comes, accept it mindfully — don’t try to hold up a building that is already falling.
koan: When lightning strikes, the ego shatters; what remains is the truth.
universalUpright: Sudden upheaval, revelation, collapse of false structures
universalReversed: Averted disaster, fear of change, delayed collapse
integration: Aligned, with a moral edge: what falls was built on something false. In a reading, ask which foundation was never sound.

name: The Star
tagline: A simple life in tune with nature brings coolness and peace to the heart.
meaning: A young warrior in white and indigo robes sits relaxed beside a sacred stream, both hands open to receive small starlights drifting down; the night sky is wide open above. New hope after crisis, healing of inner wounds, serenity, and living without forcing nature.
caution: Optimism sliding into idealistic daydreaming, or passive living — waiting on luck without moving, and missing real opportunities.
koan: When the mind is calm, even a small starlight leads to great peace.
universalReversed: Despair, disconnection, loss of faith, idle wishing
integration: The book ties the Star to wu wei — receiving rather than grasping — and immediately adds the balance: wu wei is non-forcing, not non-doing.

name: The Moon
tagline: The moon: illusion and anxiety.
meaning: A young warrior in dull white robes stands half-turned, gazing ahead through a night of thick mist and indigo forest. The world of illusion: uncertainty, anxiety, hidden fears, suspicion, and circumstances that are still murky.
caution: Letting dark moods, scattered thoughts and overthinking cover true intuition. Beware silent dangers, beautiful illusions with hidden motives, and betrayal from what you cannot yet see in the dark.
koan: Moonlight casts illusions; a calm mind separates truth from fear.
universalUpright: Illusion, fear, anxiety, the subconscious, uncertainty
universalReversed: Clarity returning, fear released, truths revealed
integration: Aligned. The key phrase gives a method: not to escape the moonlight but to sort fear from fact within it.

name: The Sun
tagline: The light of awakening — wisdom’s light driving away darkness.
meaning: A young warrior in gold-embroidered white robes lifts his face, eyes closed, arms spread to receive the light as golden rays drive off mist and shadow. Success, clarity and awakening: problems resolved, and life full of creative energy, happiness and warm glory.
caution: Confidence tipping into vanity and ego, outshining others and making enemies unawares. Light that is too strong dazzles — stay humble even at your peak.
koan: When the light of wisdom shines, all illusion and darkness dissolve.
integration: The Rider-Waite child on a horse becomes an adult warrior: joy framed as enlightenment rather than innocence. It is the direct answer to the Moon.

name: Judgement
tagline: The day the spirit is woken to know the truth.
meaning: A celestial being or guru freed from the flesh floats above the clouds in a golden dharma halo, blowing an ancient horn that echoes through the valleys; seekers meditating on the rocks open their eyes and wake from delusion. Liberation from old bonds — and the day of reckoning, receiving the results of one’s actions.
caution: Ignoring your instinct or your elders’ teaching; repeating the same mistakes without learning, stuck in a cycle of suffering. Now every truth comes into view, and the results of actions can no longer be twisted or escaped.
koan: When the horn sounds, the sleeping mind awakens and all karma is revealed.
universalReversed: Self-doubt, refusing the call, harsh self-judgement
integration: The same trumpet-and-rising structure as Rider-Waite, but the risen are meditators waking from delusion — resurrection read as enlightenment.

name: The World
tagline: Attaining the highest truth; life merging with the universe.
meaning: An enlightened warrior sits cross-legged on a sacred stone above the water, face serene, body radiating shimmering light. Complete and highest success: the goal reached, life in balance, prosperous and happy in both worldly and spiritual terms.
caution: At the summit, clinging to perfection breeds fear of beginning again or of change. When one cycle completes, a new one — the Fool — is always ready to begin.
koan: When the mind becomes one, it is full, complete, calm and cool.
universalReversed: Incompletion, lack of closure, delays, shortcuts
integration: The book explicitly loops the World back to the Fool — the Taoist circle. Reads the same as in Rider-Waite.

name: Ace of Pentacles
tagline: Saving and working hard to become your parents’ support in the future.
meaning: An auspicious start full of stability and wealth — a golden chance to build yourself up, guided by good intentions and gratitude. A real commitment to begin saving and working in earnest, with the goal of becoming the pillar for your parents and family.
caution: A good opportunity means nothing without continuous action. Don’t let progress stay on paper; keep strict self-discipline and resist temptations that would shake your long-term finances.
koan: The first coin of diligence is the foundation of the family’s future security.
universalUpright: New financial opportunity, prosperity, a seed, manifestation
universalReversed: Lost opportunity, poor planning, scarcity mindset
integration: The same seed-of-wealth card, with a purpose written into it: the wealth is for the people who depend on you.

name: Two of Pentacles
tagline: Balancing time, income and expenses while caring for elders at home.
meaning: Adaptability and keeping life running smoothly through wise allocation of time and money. Responsibility for building your own future alongside caring for family, dividing resources carefully.
caution: Carrying so much you lose control. Avoid overspending or high-risk investment now, always keep a financial backup, and never overlook the family’s regular expenses.
koan: Financial balance lets us grow without leaving anyone behind.
integration: Identical — the deck simply names the two things being juggled: your own future and your parents’ needs.

name: Three of Pentacles
tagline: Learning professional skills diligently and turning knowledge into income for the family.
meaning: Perseverance, self-development and building the future through expertise: studying, practising, and working with specialists to raise your ability, then turning knowledge into tangible work, assets and income that ease the family’s load.
caution: Don’t stop until you are truly expert. Beware the pride of “I already know” that shuts out experienced advice, or neglecting teamwork. Listen and exchange knowledge.
koan: Deep, genuine professional mastery is the tool for earning to care for the family.
universalReversed: Poor teamwork, lack of skill, ignoring input

name: Four of Pentacles
tagline: Thrift and saving to cover medical costs when parents fall ill.
meaning: Protecting security and managing resources tightly: careful spending and serious saving. Here that becomes gratitude — building an emergency fund for elders’ welfare and medical care.
caution: Fixating on the balance until you turn stingy or anxious — holding on too tight. Saving is good, but in balance: don’t deny yourself basic happiness or burden those around you.
koan: Saving with love is a shield for those who raised you.
universalReversed: Greed, hoarding — or overspending; financial insecurity
integration: The universal Four leans toward possessiveness; this deck redeems it by giving the hoard a purpose. Ask whether the holding-on serves someone or merely soothes fear.

name: Five of Pentacles
tagline: Hardship shared as a family — the test of children who do not abandon their parents.
meaning: Poverty, crisis, and physical and emotional hardship; a family facing life’s storms and financial strain together. The great test of true filial piety: the loyalty to stay hand in hand without abandoning one another.
caution: Don’t let despair, self-pity or outside stress erode your unity. Don’t stare so hard at the darkness that you miss a way out or help close by; economise together and solve problems with a clear mind.
koan: Share the good times, never desert in the bad — gratitude in hardship is the core of life.
universalReversed: Recovery, help arriving, the end of hard times
integration: The Rider-Waite image shows two figures passing a lit window, help unnoticed. The book’s caution makes the same point: look for the door that is already open.

name: Six of Pentacles
tagline: Regularly giving money, food and necessities to parents and benefactors.
meaning: Generosity, balanced sharing and giving back; you are stable enough to help others. The merit of gratitude: setting aside money, goods and essentials to honour and support parents and benefactors consistently.
caution: Giving that tips out of balance. Help others — even family — only without putting yourself in trouble. Check your means before you give, and don’t give expecting a return.
koan: The grateful giver’s hand stands high and overflows with prosperity.
universalUpright: Generosity, charity, giving and receiving, fairness

name: Seven of Pentacles
tagline: Watching success bear fruit, and planning to share it with those who gave you life.
meaning: Harvest, long-term perseverance and assessing growth; pride in the results of long effort. A moment to pause and plan how to share the profit back with your parents.
caution: Impatience, or stopping out of passing satisfaction. Results are showing, but building security isn’t finished — don’t blow the lump sum; keep discipline and plan the split.
koan: The fruit of effort is loveliest when returned to nourish your benefactors.

name: Eight of Pentacles
tagline: Meticulous, diligent work to build your own standing.
meaning: Industry, specialised mastery and relentless skill-building, with care in every detail. Building a stable future through your own effort, determined to secure your position as soon as possible.
caution: Overworking and neglecting your health; so absorbed in the work or the money that you miss precious time with loved ones. Balance your time to keep body and spirit creating.
koan: One piece crafted with care is one step toward lasting stability.

name: Nine of Pentacles
tagline: Secure financial success that makes your parents proud and free of worry.
meaning: Abundance, independence and high financial goals reached by your own effort; stable, self-reliant wealth. Tangible success that makes parents and elders deeply proud and releases all their worry.
caution: “Loneliness at the summit”: so focused on success and money that you neglect relationships. Beware arrogance in affluence; celebrate with humility.
koan: Firm, self-made success is the reward that sets your parents’ hearts at rest.

name: Ten of Pentacles
tagline: Family warmth — descendants caring for elders, inheriting both wealth and bonds.
meaning: Complete success and the highest, most solid security; prosperity passed from generation to generation — the peak of material filial piety. The extended family gathers in the ancestral house around its elders, inheriting a precious legacy and tight bonds.
caution: Family disputes over money. Attachment to assets or expectations of inheritance can spoil the atmosphere at home. Put feelings first; keep communication transparent and fair.
koan: The greatest inheritance is not vast wealth but warm family bonds.
universalUpright: Legacy, family wealth, inheritance, long-term success
universalReversed: Family conflict, financial loss, inheritance disputes
integration: The book’s caution is exactly the universal reversed meaning.

name: Page of Pentacles
tagline: The good-hearted child who studies hard so parents can rejoice in the results.
meaning: Eagerness, beginning to learn, laying the groundwork for the future with a sincere heart. Diligence, patience and self-discipline, driven by the noble wish to make your parents proud and happy.
caution: Failure from following whims without follow-through, or being all theory and no experience. Focus on one thing at a time, be careful with detail, and accumulate real experience.
koan: Every sincere effort to learn is a precious gift.
universalUpright: Study, ambition, a new venture, manifestation
universalReversed: Procrastination, lack of progress, learning without doing

name: Knight of Pentacles
tagline: Committed, honest, building life’s foundation step by step for the family.
meaning: Diligence, high responsibility and steady, unshakeable progress — the committed child who works hard with honesty first. Gratitude shown not in fine words but in real deeds that bring lasting security to the family.
caution: Stubbornness, clinging to old methods, or moving too slowly from excess caution. Sometimes you must open to change and new chances; don’t let the weight of duty drain the life from life.
koan: Every steady, honest step builds a foundation that never collapses.

name: Queen of Pentacles
tagline: Running the household — meals, hygiene and comfort.
meaning: Abundance, generosity and compassionate caretaking; gratitude through meticulous support. Keeping the home peaceful and attending to the food, hygiene and physical comfort of parents so they can rest somewhere warm and safe.
caution: Worry and fussy micromanaging born of too much goodwill. Arranging every detail of others’ lives smothers them; care with the right distance and let each person decide their own affairs.
koan: Your parents’ warmth and smiles are the true wealth of a grateful child.

name: King of Pentacles
tagline: Head of the family — a pillar steady as a mountain, keeping the whole clan safe and well.
meaning: The highest success, complete wealth and powerful asset management — the family leader at the top of his path. A pillar steady as a mountain, shouldering broad responsibility and spreading his branches to shelter and support the clan and its dependants.
caution: Attachment to things, power or control until you become autocratic and inflexible. Temper power with kindness, listen, and don’t let workaholism wear you down.
koan: A leader’s greatest success is to be a steady, cooling shade.

name: Ace of Cups
tagline: Love and bonding; a heart full of heartfelt gratitude.
meaning: The beginning of noble feeling, a flow of true love and spiritual peace — the pure bond we are born with. A heart brimming with awareness of what we have been given; the power of compassion and forgiveness that overflows to nourish and heal yourself and those around you.
caution: Emotion overriding reason. Don’t pour out feeling or expect warmth from others so much that you end up hurt. Build emotional resilience.
koan: Pure love and knowing gratitude are a spring of happiness that never runs dry.
universalUpright: New love, compassion, emotional beginnings, intuition
universalReversed: Blocked or repressed feeling, emptiness, self-love needed
integration: Aligned — the overflowing cup is filled specifically with gratitude.

name: Two of Cups
tagline: Opening up and exchanging feelings with love, understanding and no prejudice.
meaning: Reconciliation, tuning emotional frequencies, and alliances built on equality. Breaking down inner walls; honest communication driven by empathy, laying down pride and bias to listen and embrace each other’s differences.
caution: Giving in until you lose your ground, or talk that soothes but doesn’t fix the root cause. Clear the air frankly but gently, and don’t dig up the past to judge the present.
koan: Lay down bias and listen — the threads will weave the family into one.
integration: The universal Two of Cups is usually romantic; here it extends to any reconciliation, especially across generations.

name: Three of Cups
tagline: Celebration and the laughter of the young.
meaning: Joy, unity and shared happiness — a festive family gathering with everyone present. Pure joy born of bonds; the bright energy of the young is an elixir that keeps elders youthful and long-lived.
caution: So much revelry that you neglect core responsibilities. Manage time and balance, protect your plans and long-term health, and watch entertainment spending.
koan: Warm laughter is the finest elixir of long life.

name: Four of Cups
tagline: Examining your own heart — boredom and cold displays of emotion.
meaning: Stopping to reflect; satiation, sinking mood, discontent with what is. A tired mind that starts shutting others out. Gratitude here means looking deeply at yourself and catching the mood before it leaks out as coldness that wounds without meaning to.
caution: Retreating into your private world and negativity until you ignore the good things and chances being offered. A sulky face or silence can crack close relationships; when you’re not ready, politely step away to meditate and reset.
koan: Know the boredom in your own heart, to keep warmth and smiles alive.
universalReversed: Renewed interest, acceptance, stepping out of withdrawal
integration: The universal card points at the offer you’re ignoring; this deck turns the lens on the effect your mood has on others. Use both: notice the hand holding out the cup, and notice your own face.

name: Five of Cups
tagline: Drowning in loss — conscience urging you to turn back and care for family.
meaning: Grief, disappointment and dwelling on what has passed; a gloomy, pessimistic view of crisis. Mindfulness pulls you to accept reality, let go of longing, see new chances — and above all to turn back and embrace and care for your family.
caution: Letting sorrow and attachment to the past eat at you until you ignore what’s good now. Staying in pain too long blinds you to the love and hope around you; come back to the present and look for healing.
koan: Don’t be so busy mourning what’s lost that you forget the family beside you.
universalReversed: Acceptance, moving on, forgiveness, finding what remains
integration: The Rider-Waite figure mourns three spilled cups while two still stand behind him. This deck names those two standing cups: your family.

name: Six of Cups
tagline: The card of gratitude — remembering, never forgetting the past, going home to visit and care.
meaning: Beautiful memories, bonds with the past, returning to your roots — the deck’s truest card of gratitude. The virtue of not forgetting: the joy of going back to look after and visit your hometown, and of showing love and respect to the parents and benefactors who raised you.
caution: Nostalgia that makes you neglect present duties; don’t use the past as an escape from reality. Turn that love into drive for a good future.
koan: One who never forgets home has a taproot that is strong, beautiful and never withers.
universalReversed: Stuck in the past, unrealistic memories, leaving home
integration: The deck’s signature 孝 card. The universal reading gives the mood (memory, innocence); the Tao reading gives the action (go back, visit, give).

name: Seven of Cups
tagline: Staying mindful — not indulging, not forgetting duty, honouring good expectations.
meaning: Imagination, dreams and many options; a time of desire, craving and temptations that pull the mind off course. Anchor your awareness among the world’s lures; don’t give in to passing desire and forget your duty and the good hopes your parents hold for you.
caution: Stuck in fantasy — thinking but never doing — or swayed by outside stimuli until you lose your stance. What looks good may be an illusion leading you astray. Cut the unnecessary and focus on one goal as your compass.
koan: See through illusions mindfully; hold to duty so hope doesn’t crumble.

name: Eight of Cups
tagline: Sacrifice — travelling far on a mission for a better future.
meaning: Turning your back on the old to seek something better; leaving familiarity and present comfort. A resolute willingness to sacrifice personal happiness, overcome loneliness and travel far from home to new lands for a greater duty and a better future.
caution: Sadness, homesickness or loneliness sapping morale. This journey may bring loneliness to you and to the elders left behind. Stay firm in your original purpose.
koan: Turn from today’s comfort to carry the mission of a better tomorrow.
universalUpright: Walking away, disillusionment, seeking deeper meaning
universalReversed: Fear of change, aimless drifting, staying too long
integration: The universal Eight leaves what no longer satisfies; the Tao Eight leaves for a duty — working abroad to support the family, say. Surrounding cards decide which.

name: Nine of Cups
tagline: Contentment — ease of body and mind in your way of life.
meaning: Deep satisfaction, emotional fulfilment and personal enjoyment; a life settled enough to be fully self-reliant. The security that brings the deepest contentment — especially to parents who watch their children stand on their own, happy and stable.
caution: Vanity, carelessness, or basking in comfort until you stop growing. Keep up effort and virtue; use this worry-free time to share joy and care for your elders.
koan: A life of ease in which you can look after yourself is the highest contentment.

name: Ten of Cups
tagline: A flourishing home — emotional fulfilment where the whole family loves and lives together.
meaning: True happiness, emotional abundance and the highest success in family life — “a house prospers when those within live in harmony.” Every generation, from grandparents to grandchildren, bound in love and understanding.
caution: Optimism that ignores outside change, or keeping up appearances and sweeping small problems under the rug. Tend the warmth consistently; don’t let familiarity make you overlook how people at home feel.
koan: When a household is loving and united, everything in life prospers.
integration: Echoes the Chinese proverb 家和萬事興 — harmony at home, prosperity in all things.

name: Page of Cups
tagline: The sweet-natured child — gentle words and small gifts that make parents smile.
meaning: Tenderness, a pure heart and lovely emotional expression — the gentle, attentive child. Gratitude in its warmest form: bringing brightness home through caring words and small, sincere gifts that move the heart.
caution: Emotional over-sensitivity, tears at every turn, or being swept away by momentary feeling. Soft-heartedness can be exploited. Don’t decide big matters on emotion, and be wary of sweet talk.
koan: Sweet words and gifts from a pure heart are nectar to the soul.
universalUpright: Creative spark, intuitive message, curiosity, sensitivity

name: Knight of Cups
tagline: Bringer of love and peace; healer of hearts.
meaning: Messenger of good news, emotional grace, and a life led by beautiful ideals — the artistic child with a sensitive, empathic heart. An ambassador of culture and family love who brings calm, relaxation and good news, soothing and dispelling sorrow.
caution: Artistic moodiness without seriousness, or escaping into ideals away from practical reality. Without firmness and concrete responsibility, plans drift with the mood.
koan: Good news and gentleness are heavenly medicine for a weary heart.
universalUpright: Romance, charm, invitation, following the heart

name: Queen of Cups
tagline: Full of empathy — listening to suffering with patience and gentleness.
meaning: Deep compassion, emotional healing and a steady refuge; unconditional love. Receiving and listening patiently to every sorrow, hurt and stress of each person in the home — the great sheltering tree that carries the family through crisis.
caution: Absorbing others’ pain until you suffer alongside them. If you can’t separate their feelings from yours, you will break and run dry. Practise empathy without sinking, and make time to recover.
koan: A gentle embrace and heartfelt listening are the safest harbour.
integration: The book’s caution is the classic reversed Queen of Cups.

name: King of Cups
tagline: The emotional centre — excellent self-control and emotional stability.
meaning: The highest emotional maturity: composure, depth, and compassion as wide as the ocean. The elder — or child — at the heart of the family; calm, reassuring, a fortress of steadiness when emotions run high.
caution: Suppressing feelings under a calm mask until they become an emotional time bomb, or being so kind that you lack decisiveness when reason must act. Find healthy outlets, and pair kindness with real fairness.
koan: A mind calm as the ocean is the safest refuge in an emotional storm.

name: Ace of Swords
tagline: Wisdom and decisiveness to cut off problems before they cause harm.
meaning: The birth of mental power, victory over obstacles, and truth cutting through confusion; wise, decisive action on what is right. Moral resolve and awakened gratitude, ready to sever toxic ties and intoxications and end drawn-out situations without hesitation, pre-empting trouble.
caution: Harshness, temper and cutting words that become aggression. Without gentleness and understanding, the blade turns back to wound those closest to you. Discern right from wrong calmly.
koan: The sword of wisdom cuts every problem free of trouble.
universalUpright: Clarity, breakthrough, truth, a new idea

name: Two of Swords
tagline: Controlling emotion across the generation gap — choosing calm over confrontation.
meaning: Holding balance in a no-win situation; pausing to reflect and compromise amid clashing views between generations. Great forbearance: choosing to stay still, hold back harsh words and not retaliate, to avoid an emotional clash and keep the peace.
caution: Covering eyes and ears and refusing to choose until things escalate; silence that only cuts the matter short without real understanding. Don’t ignore it for long — use the calm to settle everyone, then wait for the right moment.
koan: Stay still to quiet the clash between generations; guard the heart by governing emotion.
universalReversed: Indecision exposed, information overload, finally choosing
integration: The universal reading warns the blindfold is avoidance; the book honours it as restraint — but only as a pause. The useful question: am I being patient, or hiding?

name: Three of Swords
tagline: Sorrow from conflict — learning from pain to heal the relationship.
meaning: Emotional wounds, deep disappointment, and pain from words or deeds that pierce — sorrow from conflict at home. Wisdom to accept and learn from the pain honestly, not to wallow or resent, but to change behaviour, lower pride and hurry to mend a fragile bond.
caution: Temper, sarcasm, spite, and dredging up past faults to hurt each other until the crack spreads. Separate to cool down at once; then talk openly with reason and maturity.
koan: Learn from the pain of the crack, so the bond becomes lasting.
integration: Aligned, but this deck steers heartbreak toward repair rather than separation.

name: Four of Swords
tagline: Rest — quiet words, quiet mind, releasing stress.
meaning: A temporary pause to restore body and spirit, withdrawing from chaos to heal. Knowing your own emotional state and setting stress and outside problems aside for a while, so that murky or negative energy doesn’t spill onto the people at home.
caution: Suppressing problems or escaping reality by putting things off until it’s too late. Don’t give up or abandon responsibility for good. Recharge fully, and face things again once calm and ready.
koan: Quiet words, a quiet heart at home — let the stress go.

name: Five of Swords
tagline: Defeating your parents with words — satisfying, but a grave wrong.
meaning: Conflict, stubborn pride and an empty victory won by wounding words and emotion — beating your parents in an argument. Reflect, lay down your weapons, drop pride and ego entirely, and protect your elders’ feelings; forcing a win over those who raised you with disrespectful logic brings only sorrow.
caution: Letting momentary emotion and the need to be right wreck the feelings of those who love you most. When you disagree, breathe, step back and listen humbly. Yielding and silence are not defeat.
koan: To beat your parents with cutting words is a moral defeat.
universalUpright: Conflict, hollow victory, winning at all costs, betrayal
integration: The clearest case of the deck narrowing a universal card. For non-family questions keep the universal core: a win that costs the relationship is a loss.

name: Six of Swords
tagline: Steering through crisis to safety with a calm heart.
meaning: Problems easing, crossing life’s storms and moving gradually toward better conditions. The great task of guiding everyone at home through crisis — responsibility as calm perseverance, like a helmsman steering steadily through strong wind and waves.
caution: Discouragement, fatigue, or impatience for instant results that mistimes the fix. Keep steady, manage your emotions, hold to calm and to what is right, and this storm will pass.
koan: Steer calmly and carry every life through the storm to a safe shore.
universalUpright: Transition, moving on, calmer waters, travel
universalReversed: Stuck in transition, unfinished business, resistance

name: Seven of Swords
tagline: Using wit and quick thinking to solve problems.
meaning: Strategy, ingenuity and manoeuvring to get through a hard situation. Carrying and protecting: quietly and carefully using your wits to resolve obstacles yourself — with the pure aim that your elders won’t worry or overthink to the detriment of their health.
caution: Carrying problems alone beyond your strength, or methods so opaque and cunning that they breed suspicion when the truth comes out. Use cleverness in the right way, and consult your elders.
koan: Use your wits to resolve problems; carry the truth so no one has to worry.
universalUpright: Deception, stealth, strategy, getting away with something
universalReversed: Coming clean, conscience, exposure, rethinking the approach
integration: The biggest divergence in the deck. Rider-Waite reads theft and deceit; the book reads discreet, protective problem-solving — yet its own caution circles back to the risk of secrecy. Read it as “strategy” and let neighbouring cards decide whether that strategy protects or deceives.

name: Eight of Swords
tagline: Trapped in a frame — using wisdom to find the way out slowly, without judging from emotion.
meaning: Constraint, limitation and feeling stuck — trapped by family rules or problems that feel like darkness on every side. Use calm intelligence to look for the exit patiently; these frames are often built by your own thoughts and anxieties.
caution: Letting worry, fear or old conventions bind you until you can’t move and give in to the problem. Accept the limits that are real now, listen respectfully, and untie each knot creatively and maturely.
koan: In the frame of family problems, wisdom and calm are the key to the way out.
integration: Aligned — both systems stress that the bindings are looser than they feel.

name: Nine of Swords
tagline: Anxiety and stress about health — the sign of a deeply caring heart.
meaning: Mental suffering, accumulated stress and circling thoughts at night — anxiety about a parent’s health and wellbeing. It isn’t born of ill will but of love’s dark side turning into fear: a child so bonded to those who raised them that fear of the future keeps them awake.
caution: Sinking into fear beyond reason until it erodes your own health; your anxiety can also spread tension at home. Turn the stress into action in the present rather than overthinking.
koan: When care turns into stress, transform worry into strength.
integration: A compassionate reframe of the universal card: the fear exists because the love does.

name: Ten of Swords
tagline: Rock bottom of crisis or loss — accept reality and rise to fight again.
meaning: The end of an extreme crisis, the lowest point — the nadir of a crisis or loss in the family. When darkness passes, light always returns; painful and hard to accept, but also a sign of a new beginning, met with mature acceptance of the loss.
caution: Wallowing in grief, losing the will to go on, or denial that forfeits a fresh start. Accept what is lost, release past failure, tend your own heart, and prepare for a new dawn.
koan: At rock bottom there is nothing left to fear — accept the truth and rise again.
universalUpright: Painful ending, rock bottom, betrayal, crisis
universalReversed: Recovery, regeneration, the worst is over

name: Page of Swords
tagline: The alert one — watching over safety and seeing through scams.
meaning: Alertness, eagerness, quick wit and smart vigilance. Proactive protection: watching over the family’s safety in every respect, acting as a shield that warns of scams, fraudsters and dangers of the digital age — out of deep care.
caution: Alarm beyond reason, or coming across as harsh, aggressive and nagging until it turns into fault-finding at home. Pair vigilance with humility; explain dangers with facts and a gentle tone.
koan: Watch with quick wit and see through every scam — with a caring heart.
integration: A modern touch: the book explicitly casts this Page as the one protecting elders from online scams.

name: Knight of Swords
tagline: Ready to charge — brave and resolute, protecting family from injustice.
meaning: Speed, force, surging ahead and attacking problems fearlessly — the brave, decisive child. A protective knight ready to charge, stand in front and spread his wings over parents and household at once, undaunted by any hardship.
caution: Recklessness, ferocity and haste without care. Pair resolve with wisdom, plan before you charge, and avoid harsh words when negotiating.
koan: The sword of courage is ready to charge — protecting with resolve and loyalty.

name: Queen of Swords
tagline: Upright, resolute and reasonable — caring, and counselling with humility.
meaning: Sharp intelligence, decisive maturity, and justice above emotion. Gratitude grounded in right view — caring for parents on the basis of what is right — and the courage to be a true friend who counsels and corrects everyone in the family humbly and sincerely, protecting its name and peace.
caution: Hard reasoning and cold logic becoming coldness that hurts elders without meaning to. Lead with understanding and gentleness before logic; keep your manner and speech respectful.
koan: Upright and reasonable, dare to counsel — with humility.
universalUpright: Clear boundaries, independence, direct communication, perception

name: King of Swords
tagline: A leader who uses justice, wisdom and right rules to solve problems.
meaning: The highest authority, integrity, and a steady intellectual pillar — a leader who uses fairness, wisdom and correct rules to settle family matters. Honesty and inner virtue: the decisive judge holding to moral rightness, rules and facts without emotion, bias or favouritism.
caution: Power held too tightly, autocracy, or rules enforced until they destroy feelings and bonds. Running a home is not commanding an army — blend decisiveness with mercy and reason grounded in what is right.
koan: Hold to wisdom and fair rules — decisive and free of emotional bias.

name: Ace of Wands
tagline: Igniting resolve; taking up the family enterprise.
meaning: A powerful beginning, inspiration taking form, the dawn of creative success. Pure, awakened fire: taking the baton to carry on the ancestors’ business or ideals, entering a new era with confidence, ready to shoulder the mission and turn drive into concrete prosperity.
caution: Impatience; a straw fire that blazes and dies fast; insisting on your own way while ignoring the foundations and teachings of those before you. Plan long-term and step carefully.
koan: Ignite resolve; carry your ancestors’ purpose to glory.
universalReversed: Delays, lack of direction, false start
integration: Aligned, with a lineage twist: the spark is often inherited.

name: Two of Wands
tagline: Planning the future; raising your standing and honour.
meaning: Broad vision, foresight, and the first step toward new growth — planning to extend your success. Stable enough, but not standing still: spreading out the map of life and business to find new routes, even abroad, to raise the family’s standing, stature and honour.
caution: Hesitating until you miss the golden chance, or planning on paper without ever acting. Use the information and vision you have to decide firmly, then execute systematically.
koan: Spread the map of life with far-seeing vision, for honour and a glorious standing.
universalReversed: Fear of the unknown, lack of planning, playing safe

name: Three of Wands
tagline: Facing the wide world with parents’ teachings as your inner compass.
meaning: Progress, proactive departure, and watching effort begin to bear fruit — stepping into the world with confidence. Building for the future, rooted in your parents’ teaching as an inner compass and moral anchor that gives you the courage to meet every new opportunity and challenge.
caution: Complacency, or expecting results too fast and losing care amid volatile conditions. Losing discipline or forgetting elders’ counsel can trip up your future. Stay committed, honest and alert.
koan: Step out to face the world with pride, teachings as your compass.

name: Four of Wands
tagline: Building stability and bringing pride home to honour the family.
meaning: Lasting success, celebration of victory, and the peace of a life well founded; stable work that lets you settle. Perseverance arriving somewhere permanent, and bringing great pride home as honour and prosperity for the family line.
caution: Resting on past success until you grow careless and stop developing. Real success needs ongoing maintenance; celebrate warmly with family, and manage this stability so it lasts.
koan: Stable through wisdom — establish pride as honour for the family.
universalReversed: Transition, lack of support, conflict at home

name: Five of Wands
tagline: Outside conflict and competition — never doing anything corrupt that would stain the family.
meaning: Struggle amid obstacles and fierce competition in the outside world. Standing on virtue and teaching: however hard competitors or circumstances press, you hold to what is right and never stoop to corruption or anything that would disgrace your name.
caution: Being pulled into the surrounding conflict until you lose your head, or retaliating eye for an eye. Let stillness subdue the commotion, and keep your ideals pure.
koan: Amid competition and storms of conflict, hold firm to your principles.
integration: Aligned; the book adds an integrity test to the rivalry.

name: Six of Wands
tagline: Passing exams, promotion, winning with integrity — bringing honour to the family.
meaning: Tangible victory and great success after long toil, with public recognition. The deepest pride: overcoming obstacles by genuine ability without shortcuts, and bringing name, honour and joy to the family.
caution: Revelling in fame and rank, or arrogance after victory. Virtue and humility are what keep you in the position; hold your moral standard firm.
koan: Win by pure virtue, bringing the highest name and honour.
universalReversed: Ego, fall from grace, lack of recognition

name: Seven of Wands
tagline: Courage — defending your good name and fighting through without surrender.
meaning: Grit, holding the high ground, and fighting life’s battles to protect what matters. The spirit of a fighter: under pressure and attack from every side, you won’t give a single step, shouldering heavy duty to defend the family’s honour.
caution: Accumulated stress and exhaustion from being the front line alone. Fighting without rest or refusing help leads to burnout; manage your energy and keep your advantage.
koan: Stand on what is right; step forward to defend the family’s honour.
universalUpright: Defence, perseverance, standing your ground, challenge

name: Eight of Wands
tagline: Rapid progress at work — parents relieved and proud of their child’s ability.
meaning: Speed, leaps of growth, and positive energy surging ahead unobstructed. Effort answered by heaven and earth: projects and opportunities pour in suddenly, bringing stability and prosperity and raising happiness at home.
caution: Haste without care; taking on too many tasks at once and slipping on detail. Vague communication can cause misunderstanding; keep your wits and your consistency.
koan: Work surges ahead, bringing relief and settling pride in the heart.

name: Nine of Wands
tagline: Exhausted and burdened, yet standing firm in duty.
meaning: Supreme endurance, a heavy burden, and pride in duty even when drained. After countless battles and nearly spent, you still stand firm without abandoning your post — still guarding the family’s shared business (the kongsi) and protecting its security with utmost responsibility.
caution: Accumulated stress, over-vigilance, or insisting on carrying everything alone until the body gives out. Pushing on while exhausted harms your health long-term; rest to recover.
koan: The body may tire of its burdens, but the heart still stands to its duty.
universalUpright: Resilience, persistence, a last stand, boundaries
integration: Aligned. The “kongsi” — the Chinese-Thai family business and shared purse — is a distinctly local touch.

name: Ten of Wands
tagline: Carrying the burden — forbearance and toil.
meaning: The highest responsibility, hard labour and outstanding endurance. The peak of a strong, resolute mind that gives up personal comfort, pouring sweat and strength into supporting parents and household so they live well and have a good future.
caution: Carrying every task alone beyond your limits of body and mind. If you collapse, the family behind you loses its support and suffers more. Learn to share the load, delegate, and rest to preserve yourself.
koan: Carrying hopes and expenses — willing to toil, with patience and a glad heart.
universalReversed: Delegation, release, letting go of burdens
integration: The caution supplies the practical logic behind the universal reversal: your collapse hurts the very people you are carrying.

name: Page of Wands
tagline: Boundless energy, a love of learning, improving life.
meaning: Awakening to study, fresh inspiration, and leading creative change. The gratitude of a new generation: a child devoted to worldly knowledge, technology and many disciplines, with the pure aim of bringing knowledge and innovation home to improve the family’s life and modernise the family enterprise.
caution: Getting bored easily — brief excitement over something new, then dropping it with nothing to show — or forcing modern tools and ideas so abruptly that you clash with elders’ ways. Present new ideas with humility.
koan: Learn with boundless energy; bring innovation and creativity home to improve life.

name: Knight of Wands
tagline: Fired up, committed, proactive and hard-working.
meaning: Aspiration, powerful drive and surging forward with confidence — the child with fire and resolve. A new generation full of proactive energy, ready to fight hard in life and work, driven to establish yourself, raise your standing and bring home tangible success with pride.
caution: Impatience and recklessness that cause mistakes in detail or straw-fire efforts. Keep the flame, listen to objections and warnings, and don’t overdo the work.
koan: Work proactively with the fire of resolve, and make success evident.

name: Queen of Wands
tagline: A capable woman who runs work efficiently while keeping the family in order.
meaning: All-round ability, self-confidence and excellent management. A highly responsible leader who balances life remarkably — steering the family business or career to growth while keeping everything at home in order and creating warmth and stability for everyone.
caution: Wanting everything under your command, or a strict, autocratic manner that stifles the family. Too much tightness breeds conflict; govern with gentleness alongside decisiveness.
koan: Decisive and efficient at work; gentle in caring for family.

name: King of Wands
tagline: A leader of vision, presence and virtue, bringing prosperity to the family line.
meaning: The highest success as a ruler: stability, and authority softened by mercy. The peak of responsibility as the family’s pillar — rising to the top through genuine ability and bringing abundance, honour and lasting peace to everyone at home.
caution: Self-confidence that hardens into stubbornness and not listening, or overworking to build prestige while neglecting health and close relationships. Pair presence with humility, and give the younger generation room to show their skill.
koan: Rule by virtue, lead by vision, live as a beautiful example.
